item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00076","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C09","C21","C19"],"selected_candidate_label":"C09","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C09 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both letters ask Congress to authorize a specified United States contribution to a United Nations humanitarian program, explain the program's General Assembly basis and funding need, describe a shift from immediate relief toward durable development in underdeveloped regions, invoke both American humanitarian ideals and the national interest, and close by urging early congressional action. C21 and C19 are closely related to the same children's-welfare authority, but their short delegations of executive functions do not provide the child's legislative-request structure or developed argument.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am writing to ask that the Congress authorize a contribution of twelve million dollars by the United States to the International Children's Emergency Fund.","parent_excerpt":"I am transmitting herewith for the consideration of the Congress a draft of proposed legislation to enable the United States to participate in and contribute to the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East.","explanation":"Both open with a request for legislation authorizing a United States contribution to a named United Nations humanitarian agency."},{"child_excerpt":"The General Assembly of the United Nations, on December 1, 1950, extended the operations of the Children's Fund for a period of three years. Since the authorization to make financial contributions to the Fund expired last June 30, we can now make no further contribution without this new authority from the Congress.","parent_excerpt":"This Agency has been established by the General Assembly of the United Nations... I, therefore, recommend that the Congress authorize and appropriate $27,450,000 for an eighteen month period.","explanation":"The same administrative-legal machinery links General Assembly action, a defined program period and amount, and the need for congressional authorization and funding."},{"child_excerpt":"The main work of the Fund has now shifted from Europe to the underdeveloped areas of Asia and Latin America... to strengthen the permanent child welfare programs of the countries themselves.","parent_excerpt":"It is advantageous to combine the relief program, with the beginnings of longer range economic development... Its recommendations are an example of the kind of development and planning which is essential to the economic growth and improvement of underdeveloped areas.","explanation":"Both justify humanitarian assistance by presenting it as a bridge from immediate relief to lasting institutional or economic development in underdeveloped areas."},{"child_excerpt":"Nothing is more consistent with our basic interests or more representative of our humanitarian ideals.","parent_excerpt":"Not only is it consistent with the humanitarian spirit of the American people; it is also in our national interest","explanation":"This is a distinctive shared two-part justification based on humanitarian character and national interest."},{"child_excerpt":"It is my hope that the Congress will find it possible to give early consideration to this measure.","parent_excerpt":"I recommend to the Congress the early enactment of legislation to enable the United States to take its part in this program of the United Nations.","explanation":"Both conclude by urging prompt legislative action so the United States can support the UN program."}]}
